questions.question: A vehicle is parked at night on a public road. In which situation is it legally permitted for the vehicle’s lights to remain off?

options.text: When the vehicle is parked facing the flow of traffic
When the vehicle is parked within 12 metres of a streetlight illuminating the road
When the driver remains inside the vehicle

questions.explanation: A vehicle parked at night may have its lights off if it is parked within 12 m of a lit street lamp illuminating the road.

questions.question: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are not functioning. A traffic officer is using control hand signals to direct vehicles through the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Follow the traffic officer’s hand signals, even if they differ from the road signs or traffic lights
Obey the road signs first, since traffic lights are not operational
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop until the traffic lights are repaired

questions.explanation: A traffic officer's signals override road signs and traffic lights.

questions.question: A learner's licence becomes valid:

options.text: On the date the application is approved
On the day the learner’s test is passed
24 hours after issue

questions.explanation: A learner's licence is valid from the day the learner's test is passed.

questions.question: A traffic officer gives the hand signal shown in the diagram provided. What does this signal instruct drivers to do?

options.text: Proceed with caution, as cross traffic has been stopped
Stop only if turning at the intersection
Stop if approaching the officer from the front

questions.explanation: Officer with the right arm raised vertically: traffic approaching the officer from the front must stop.

questions.question: A vehicle is standing partly on the shoulder and partly on the roadway. Which part determines whether it is considered to be “on the road”?

options.text: The wheels only
Any part of the vehicle occupying the roadway
The driver’s position

questions.explanation: If any part of the vehicle occupies the roadway, it is considered to be on the road.

questions.question: A traffic officer gives the hand signal shown in the diagram provided. What does this signal instruct drivers to do?

options.text: Stop traffic approaching the officer from behind
Stop all traffic approaching the intersection
Allow vehicles behind the officer to proceed with caution

questions.explanation: Officer with the back to you and arm extended sideways: traffic approaching from behind must stop.

questions.question: When may a vehicle legally operate without an interior rear-view mirror?

options.text: When the rear window is tinted
When the interior mirror cannot provide a clear rear view and an exterior mirror compensates for it
Never, all vehicles must have one

questions.explanation: An interior mirror may be omitted if it cannot give a clear view to the rear and an exterior mirror compensates (fitted on the other side).

questions.question: A traffic officer gives the hand signal shown in the diagram provided. What does this signal mean?

options.text: Traffic approaching the officer from both the front and the rear must stop
Traffic approaching the officer from the front may proceed, while traffic from the rear must stop
Traffic approaching from the sides must stop before entering the intersection

questions.explanation: Officer with one arm raised and the other extended: traffic approaching from both the front and the rear must stop.

questions.question: Which vehicle is MOST likely classified as a goods vehicle?

options.text: A minibus carrying tools
A truck-tractor designed mainly to draw other vehicles
A bus transporting equipment instead of passengers

questions.explanation: A truck-tractor designed mainly to draw other vehicles is classified as a goods vehicle.

questions.question: A traffic officer gives the hand signal shown in the diagram provided. What does this signal instruct drivers to do?

options.text: Proceed only if the intersection is completely clear
Continue driving with caution, while remaining prepared to stop
Drivers facing the officer may proceed

questions.explanation: Officer with the hand raised and the back of the hand facing you: drivers facing the officer may proceed. (Answer as stated in the narration; the video does not highlight it on screen.)
